title: rules validate refuses a canon rule named by its path in a linked worktree: the install root's copy counts as a second declaration
body:
## What happens

`intent claude rules validate <path>`, given a canon rule file by its path inside a linked worktree of the Intent repository, refuses with `id <ID> is declared by 1 other rule file(s)`, because it counts the install root's copy of the same rule as a second declaration. The bats arms that validate each canon rule by path therefore red whenever the suite runs in a worktree with the dev pair as `INTENT_BIN`.

## Reproduce

In a linked worktree `tmp/wt-x` of the Intent repository, with the install root pointer (`~/.local/share/intent/home`) naming the main checkout and the dev pair's `intent`:

- `intent claude rules validate $PWD/intent/plugins/claude/rules/agnostic/highlander/RULE.md` prints `error: <worktree>/intent/plugins/claude/rules/agnostic/highlander/RULE.md: id IN-AG-HIGHLANDER-001 is declared by 1 other rule file(s)`, `1 error(s)`.
- Control: the same rule by the main checkout's path, `<main>/intent/plugins/claude/rules/agnostic/highlander/RULE.md`, prints `1 ok`.
- Control: bare `intent claude rules validate` in the worktree prints `68 ok`: the library it reads is the install root's alone.

The two paths it sees are the worktree's `<worktree>/intent/plugins/claude/rules/...` (named on the command line) and the install root's `<main>/intent/plugins/claude/rules/...` (the library the binary serves).

## Reach

The arms that red this way, all by `run_intent claude rules validate "$<PACK>_ROOT/<rule>/RULE.md"` with the root under `INTENT_PROJECT_ROOT`: the "each rule passes intent claude rules validate" arm of every rule_pack_*.bats (agnostic, author, content, elixir, lua, prose, rust, shell, swift), and rule_validator.bats' "rules validate against strong-assertions exemplar passes" and "rules validate reads a canon rule named by a relative path as that rule". On main the same files pass whole with the same pair. Pre-existing: they red identically in a worktree at a base without the change under judgement.

## Why it matters

Every bats run judged in a worktree, which is how this estate judges, carries these reds as noise, and a real rules regression would hide among them. Either the duplicate check should treat a named file whose canon-relative path matches the library's own copy as that rule (the relative-path arm already expects a canon rule named by path to be read "as that rule"), or the suite should point the library at the tree it runs in.

## The fix, specified (vc, 2026-10-25)

The duplicate check in intentsvcs `rules.rs` (the `twins` count beside "is declared by") compares absolute paths, so the same rule at two roots reads as two declarations. A rule's identity is its canon-relative path, the path under `intent/plugins/claude/rules/`: a file named on the command line whose canon-relative path equals a library file's IS that rule, and the library's copy leaves the validation set for that run; two files with different canon-relative paths and one id stay refused with the existing message. The suite pointing its library at the tree it runs in is the other option and is not taken: the validator already claims that a canon rule named by path is read as that rule (the relative-path arm states it), so the validator is where the claim is made true.

Arms, in intentsvcs' rules tests: a scratch library root and a scratch second root carrying the same relative path validate as one rule (`1 ok`); the same two roots with different relative paths and one id refuse; bare validate is unchanged. Then rule_validator.bats and rule_pack_agnostic.bats run once in a linked worktree with the dev pair as INTENT_BIN, the form this issue reproduces, to prove the arms green. Judge: the intentsvcs suite, fmt, clippy; light. Owner: cc.
